short: The first ruler of a united England, and the victor of Brunanburh.
full:
Athelstan succeeded his father Edward the Elder in 924 and was crowned at Kingston upon Thames the following year. In 927 he took York from its Norse rulers, becoming the first king to govern the whole of England, and received the submission of the Welsh, Scottish and Northumbrian rulers at Eamont.

His supremacy was challenged in 937 by a coalition of Olaf Guthfrithson of Dublin, Constantine II of Scotland and the men of Strathclyde. Athelstan destroyed them at Brunanburh, a battle whose site is still disputed but whose result was recorded in a poem preserved in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle. He standardised the coinage, legislated at great assemblies attended by magnates from across the kingdom, and married his sisters into the ruling houses of Francia and Germany. He died at Gloucester in October 939, unmarried and childless. York was lost again within weeks, and his successors took nearly twenty years to recover it.
